steps: The law of sines states a/sin A = b/sin B, because each ratio equals the diameter of the circumscribed circle.
Rearrange for b: b = a·sin B / sin A.

commonErrors.observed: Used the ratio of the angles themselves and answered 20.33.
commonErrors.likelyCause: Sides were assumed proportional to angles rather than to their sines.
commonErrors.remediation: Compare a 30° and a 60° angle: the sides are not in a 1:2 ratio, which rules out proportionality to the angles.

steps: Dropping a perpendicular from one vertex gives height h = b·sin C, so Area = ½ · a · h = ½ab·sin C.
With a right angle the formula reduces to the familiar ½ × base × height.

commonErrors.observed: Omitted the factor of ½ and answered 36.
commonErrors.likelyCause: The parallelogram area formula was used instead of the triangle one.
commonErrors.remediation: Recall the triangle is half of the parallelogram on the same two sides.

steps: The law of sines pairs a side with the angle opposite it, so it needs such a pair to be known.
The law of cosines relates all three sides to one angle, so it works when no side-angle pair is available.
With SAS or SSS there is no known side-angle opposite pair, so the law of cosines must come first.

commonErrors.observed: Reached for the law of sines when only SAS was given.
commonErrors.likelyCause: The requirement for a known side-angle opposite pair was overlooked.
commonErrors.remediation: Before choosing, check whether any side and its opposite angle are both known.

steps: The law of cosines gives c² = a² + b² − 2ab·cos C.
Because the angle is obtuse the cosine is negative, so the subtraction increases c² — the side opposite the largest angle is longest.

commonErrors.observed: Used the Pythagorean theorem and answered 50.
commonErrors.likelyCause: The triangle was assumed to be right-angled.
commonErrors.remediation: The Pythagorean theorem is the special case C = 90°, where the cosine term vanishes; check the given angle first.

scoringGuidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
masteryRule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use worked examples, explanation, error analysis, application, and a second occasion of evidence; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
remediationGuidance: law-of-cosines-side (G-SRT.10): if the learner misses these, reteach with the worked example “a = 5, b = 8, C = 60°. Find c².” and require the reasoning for each step before another attempt.
law-of-sines-side (G-SRT.11): if the learner misses these, reteach with the worked example “A = 30°, B = 45°, a = 10. Find b.” and require the reasoning for each step before another attempt.

triangle-area-from-two-sides-and-angle (G-SRT.9): if the learner misses these, reteach with the worked example “a = 8, b = 5, enclosed angle 30°. Area?” and require the reasoning for each step before another attempt.
choose-triangle-law (G-SRT.11): if the learner misses these, reteach with the worked example “Given SSS, which law?” and require the reasoning for each step before another attempt.
